description: Red Team Village at DEF CON Safe Mode focuses on offensive security operations, adversary emulation, evasion tradecraft, payload creation, physical implants, and purple teaming.

talks.title: Zero Trust: A Vision for Securing Cloud Infrastructure
talks.teaser: Vandana Verma Sehgal explores Zero Trust architectures, examining identity verification, micro-segmentation, and offensive testing in modern cloud environments.
talks.summary:
Social Engineering and Human-Oriented Security

This presentation explores social engineering attacks and human vulnerability in security systems. Topics include psychological manipulation, pretexting, credential harvesting, and how attackers exploit human nature to bypass technical defenses.

(AI summary — Claude Haiku)

talks.title: Android Malware Adventures: Evasion, Droppers, & Modern Mobile Tradecraft
talks.teaser: Kürşat Akıncı and Mert Can Coşkuner analyze modern Android malware techniques, from multi-stage droppers bypassing Google Play Protect to dynamic evasion.
talks.summary:
The Evolution of Android Mobile Malware

Android malware developers have adopted advanced evasion techniques borrowed from desktop malware, allowing malicious applications to slip past Google Play Protect and on-device antivirus scanners.

Multi-Stage Droppers and Dynamic Payload Decryption

Kürşat Akıncı and Mert Can Coşkuner dissect mobile droppers disguised as benign utilities that decrypt and load secondary APK/DEX payloads directly into memory.

Bypassing Dynamic Analysis and Sandbox Emulators

The speakers demonstrate how Android malware detects emulated analysis environments (QEMU, Frida hooks, debugger presence) to conceal malicious behavior during automated sandbox runs.

Mobile Threat Hunting and Defensive Telemetry

The presentation provides mobile security analysts with static analysis workflows, YARA signatures, and behavioral heuristics to detect evasive Android implants.

talks.title: Android Application Exploitation: Structured Assessment Methodologies
talks.teaser: Kyle Benac presents a structured methodology for auditing Android applications, analyzing hybrid frameworks, IPC intent vulnerabilities, and insecure storage.
talks.summary:
The Expanding Mobile Attack Surface

Modern Android applications frequently handle sensitive user authentication tokens, financial data, and enterprise APIs across hybrid and native codebases.

Identifying Mobile Frameworks and Architectures

Kyle Benac explains how to quickly identify whether an application is built with native Java/Kotlin, Flutter, React Native, or Xamarin to focus vulnerability analysis.

Auditing Inter-Process Communication and Exported Components

The author demonstrates inspecting AndroidManifest.xml for exported activities, broadcast receivers, and content providers vulnerable to intent injection and data leakage.

Practical Mobile Assessment Tooling and Remediation

The presentation outlines streamlined workflows using tools like jadx, Frida, and objection to accelerate mobile penetration testing.

talks.title: All of the Threats: Threat Intelligence Modeling Beyond ATT&CK
talks.teaser: Tim Wadhwa-Brown demonstrates how to construct threat intelligence models and hypotheses from first principles when standardized ATT&CK data is missing.
talks.summary:
The Strengths and Limitations of MITRE ATT&CK

While MITRE ATT&CK has unified communication between red and blue teams, it relies heavily on documented adversary TTPs and struggles when facing novel threats.

Building Threat Hypotheses from First Principles

Tim Wadhwa-Brown explores constructing predictive threat intelligence models by decomposing target systems, crown jewels, and feasible adversary objectives.

Synthesizing Adversary Motivations with Technical Attack Paths

The speaker illustrates how to map geopolitical threat actor motivations and organizational vulnerabilities into actionable adversary emulation plans.

Operationalizing Threat Models for Collaborative Defense

The presentation provides purple teams with structured methodologies for validating detection coverage against bespoke and hypothetical threat scenarios.

talks.title: 50 Shades of Sudo Abuse: Linux Privilege Escalation via Sudo Misconfigurations
talks.teaser: Tyler Boykin reviews Linux privilege escalation vectors stemming from sudoers misconfigurations, from common GTFOBins low-hanging fruit to subtle binary abuse.
talks.summary:
The Central Role of Sudo in Linux Access Control

Linux system administrators frequently grant unprivileged users specific sudo rights to run routine maintenance utilities without providing full root access.

Deconstructing Sudoers File Misconfigurations

Tyler Boykin analyzes common syntax oversights, wildcard abuses, and insecure environment variable preservation (`env_keep`, `LD_PRELOAD`) in `/etc/sudoers`.

Weaponizing Standard Binaries for Root Shells (GTFOBins)

The speaker demonstrates abusing text editors (vim, nano), pagers (less, more), scripting runtimes (python, perl), and archive utilities to break out into interactive root shells.

Hardening Guidelines and Least-Privilege Sudo Policies

The presentation provides system administrators with best practices for configuring sudoers rules, command whitelists, and auditing sudo execution logs.

talks.title: Guerrilla Red Team: Decentralizing Adversary Simulation Across the Enterprise
talks.teaser: Chris Cottrell introduces the Guerrilla Red Team methodology, empowering distributed engineering teams to act as trusted internal ethical hackers.
talks.summary:
The Bottleneck of Centralized Security Teams

Traditional enterprise security teams struggle to scale across massive software engineering fleets, resulting in delayed code reviews and missed vulnerability assessments.

Introducing the Guerrilla Red Team Methodology

Chris Cottrell proposes creating an internal mesh network of decentralized ethical hackers embedded directly within product engineering squads.

Upskilling Developers with Adversarial Mindsets

Cottrell details training programs, micro-challenges, and capture-the-flag exercises that transform software developers into proactive internal security champions.

Scaling Security IQ and Continuous Adversary Emulation

The author shares organizational blueprints for managing decentralized red teaming, measuring security ROI, and fostering a resilient security culture.

talks.title: Gray Hat SSH: SSHenanigans & Advanced Tunneling Tradecraft
talks.teaser: Evan Anderson explores advanced SSH tunneling techniques, local/remote port forwarding, SOCKS proxies, and stealthy lateral movement strategies.
talks.summary:
SSH as the Swiss Army Knife of Network Pivoting

Secure Shell (SSH) is universally trusted and enabled across enterprise servers, making it an ideal vehicle for red team lateral movement and tunneling.

Mastering Dynamic Port Forwarding and Reverse SOCKS Proxies

Evan Anderson demonstrates leveraging SSH's built-in `-D`, `-L`, and `-R` flags to establish multi-hop encrypted tunnels across segmented corporate enclaves.

Abusing SSH ControlMaster and Agent Forwarding

The speaker explains hijacking cached SSH agent sockets (`SSH_AUTH_SOCK`) and multiplexing sessions with ControlMaster to pivot without entering credentials.

Blue Team Telemetry and Hunting Anomalous SSH Tunnels

The presentation provides defenders with detection strategies to audit persistent SSH tunnels, anomalous port bindings, and suspicious client connection flags.

talks.title: Executing Red Team Scenarios: Proactive Adversary Emulation with Machine Learning
talks.teaser: Erdener Uyan and Gökberk Gülgün present an open-source machine learning framework for generating dynamic, automated red team attack scenarios.
talks.summary:
The Complexity of Scripting Realistic Attack Scenarios

Manual red team engagements require extensive operational planning to orchestrate believable multi-stage attack paths mimicking specific APT behavior.

Designing a Proactive ML Attack Generation Framework

Erdener Uyan and Gökberk Gülgün introduce an open-source tool that uses machine learning algorithms to generate realistic decision trees for adversary simulation.

Automating Multi-Stage Lateral Movement and Execution

The authors demonstrate how the framework selects optimal exploit techniques and persistence mechanisms dynamically based on discovered host telemetry.

Evaluating Blue Team Detection Coverage and Resilience

The presentation discusses measuring detection efficacy, identifying coverage gaps, and continuously training defensive response teams with automated scenarios.

talks.title: Sounds Legit: Don't Trust That Speaker - BadUSB in Audio Peripherals
talks.teaser: Mendoza and Mauro Cáseres demonstrate embedding BadUSB hardware implants inside commercial desktop speakers to silently execute keystroke injection.
talks.summary:
The Ubiquity and Stealth of BadUSB Hardware Implants

While BadUSB thumb drives are well-known, hiding keystroke injection microcontrollers inside common desktop peripherals bypasses physical security scrutiny.

Hardware Teardown and Implant Integration in Audio Speakers

Mendoza and Mauro Cáseres detail disassembling standard USB-powered desktop speakers and integrating programmable ATmega32U4 / Digispark microcontrollers.

Weaponizing USB Enumeration and Keystroke Injection

The speakers illustrate how the modified speaker presents itself to the operating system as both an audio output device and a high-speed Human Interface Device (HID) keyboard.

Defending Endpoints Against Peripheral HID Injection

The presentation reviews hardware whitelisting policies, endpoint USB device control agents, and physical security auditing to mitigate stealthy BadUSB peripherals.

talks.title: Evil Genius: Why You Shouldn't Trust That Keyboard
talks.teaser: Mauro Cáseres explores weaponized keyboards and hardware keyloggers, demonstrating how physical peripherals can be backdoored for stealthy initial access.
talks.summary:
This DEF CON talk covers evil genius: why you shouldn't trust that keyboard.

talks.title: erpwnage: A Red Team Approach to Targeting SAP Enterprise Systems
talks.teaser: Austin Marck demonstrates red team tradecraft for targeting SAP and ERP platforms, demonstrating protocol exploitation, RFC abuse, and business logic takeover.
talks.summary:
SAP and ERP Systems as High-Value Crown Jewels

Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) platforms like SAP manage critical financial records, payroll, and supply chain operations, making them prime targets for threat actors.

Deconstructing SAP Protocols and Communication Interfaces

Austin Marck analyzes the complex communication layers of SAP architectures—including SAP GUI, RFC gateways, DIAG protocols, and web services.

Executing Remote RFC Abuse and Business Logic Takeover

The speaker demonstrates discovering unauthenticated RFC functions, abusing default service users, and escalating privileges to execute operating system commands.

Hardening SAP Infrastructure and Monitoring TTPs

The presentation provides enterprise defenders with SAP security baselines, network segregation patterns, and guidance for auditing sensitive transaction logs.

talks.title: Enumerating Cloud File Storage Gems: Discovering Exposed Data Across S3, Azure, & GCP
talks.teaser: Michael Wylie details automated reconnaissance techniques to discover unauthenticated AWS S3 buckets, Azure Blob containers, and GCP storage leaks.
talks.summary:
The Risk of Unintentional Cloud Data Exposure

As enterprises migrate terabytes of internal documents and database backups to cloud object storage, misconfigured permissions frequently expose sensitive files publicly.

Automated Cloud Bucket Reconnaissance Techniques

Michael Wylie explains keyword generation heuristics, DNS permutations, and multi-cloud enumeration toolchains for finding target storage assets.

Searching Across AWS S3, Azure Blobs, and Google Cloud Storage

The author demonstrates verifying bucket ACLs, listing object keys, and searching through exposed file repositories for API credentials and PII.

Defensive Remediation and Continuous Storage Auditing

The presentation provides cloud administrators with policy enforcement templates (S3 Block Public Access, Azure Private Endpoints) and continuous monitoring scripts.

talks.title: Emulating an Adversary with Imperfect Intelligence
talks.teaser: MITRE ATT&CK lead Adam Pennington shares strategies for crafting realistic adversary emulation plans even when threat intelligence reports are incomplete or vague.
talks.summary:
The Reality of Incomplete Threat Intelligence

Public cyber threat intelligence reports rarely contain exhaustive playbooks, often leaving gaps in specific command-line arguments, tool configurations, and timelines.

Bridging the Gaps in Adversary Profiles

Adam Pennington demonstrates how purple team planners interpolate missing technical details by analyzing adversary objectives, tool capabilities, and analogous campaigns.

Structuring Emulation Plans with MITRE ATT&CK

The author explains mapping ambiguous report text into concrete ATT&CK techniques, sub-techniques, and actionable procedural tests.

Maximizing Defensive Validation and Training Value

The presentation offers practical guidance for red and blue teams to maximize the educational impact of emulation exercises despite imperfect adversary telemetry.

talks.title: dropengine: A Malleable Payload Creation Framework for EDR Evasion
talks.teaser: Gabriel Ryan introduces DropEngine, a modular framework for generating polymorphic, malleable shellcode runners designed to evade modern EDR solutions.
talks.summary:
The High Attrition Rate of Initial Access Payloads

Modern Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) solutions use automated static analysis, dynamic heuristics, and AMSI scanning to detect standard shellcode runners.

Introducing the DropEngine Modular Framework

Gabriel Ryan presents DropEngine, an extensible framework that decouples payload creation into swappable encrypters, decrypters, execution methods, and bypasses.

Implementing Advanced Process Injection and Unhooking

Ryan demonstrates configuring custom payload profiles—incorporating AMSI/ETW patching, direct syscall invocations, and stealthy memory allocation routines.

Detection Engineering for Polymorphic Shellcode Runners

The author discusses behavioral indicators, memory scanning heuristics, and kernel-mode telemetry necessary for defenders to catch malleable loaders.

talks.title: Deep Dive into Adversary Emulation: Ransomware Tradecraft & Purple Teaming
talks.teaser: SCYTHE CTO Jorge Orchilles details how to safely emulate multi-stage human-operated ransomware campaigns to test enterprise detection and response.
talks.summary:
The Rising Threat of Human-Operated Ransomware

Modern enterprise ransomware attacks involve multi-stage campaigns combining credential theft, lateral movement, data exfiltration, and coordinated encryption.

Designing Safe Ransomware Emulation Playbooks

Jorge Orchilles explains how to simulate destructive ransomware behaviors—including volume shadow copy deletion, service stopping, and simulated encryption—without risking data loss.

Executing End-to-End Emulation with SCYTHE

The speaker demonstrates orchestrating realistic ransomware emulation campaigns across Windows environments to validate EDR alerts and SOC response SLAs.

Closing Defensive Gaps with Collaborative Purple Teaming

The presentation provides blue teams with specific detection rules, telemetry checklists, and incident response runbooks to neutralize real-world ransomware outbreaks.

talks.title: Notebooks, Datasets, & Clouds for Offensive Automation & Threat Analysis
talks.teaser: Ryan Ekins demonstrates leveraging cloud-hosted Jupyter notebooks, large datasets, and serverless pipelines to automate offensive reconnaissance and analysis.
talks.summary:
The Intersection of Data Science and Offensive Security

Modern security operations generate massive datasets during reconnaissance and fuzzing, requiring scalable data processing pipelines.

Leveraging Jupyter Notebooks for Offensive Workflows

Ryan Ekins illustrates using cloud-hosted Jupyter notebooks and Python data science libraries (pandas, matplotlib) to analyze network attack surfaces.

Building Scalable Serverless Automation Pipelines

The speaker demonstrates deploying cloud functions and containers to orchestrate distributed port scans, asset discovery, and credential validation.

Operationalizing Big Data for Red and Purple Teams

The presentation showcases how data-driven automation streamlines attack planning and enables repeatable security telemetry analysis.

talks.title: What College Kids Always Get Wrong: Lessons from CCDC Red Teaming
talks.teaser: NECCDC red teamer Forrest Fuqua breaks down common defensive blunders collegiate competitors make when trying to harden already-compromised systems.
talks.summary:
The Pressure Cooker of Collegiate Cyber Defense (CCDC)

In collegiate cyber defense competitions, student blue teams are tasked with defending inherently vulnerable, legacy enterprise environments against active red teamers.

Analyzing Recurring Defensive Blunders

Forrest Fuqua reviews classic mistakes made by competitors—including attempting to patch non-critical services while default credentials and root backdoors remain active.

Prioritizing Incident Triage and System Isolation

The speaker explains why establishing basic visibility, password resets, and network segmentation must take precedence over complex software configuration changes.

Practical Advice for Aspiring Defenders and Educators

The presentation offers actionable defensive frameworks for cybersecurity students and competition coaches to improve incident triage under pressure.

talks.title: Bypass Python 3.8 Audit Hooks or Nah? Internals & Evasion
talks.teaser: Leron Gray dives into Python 3.8's PEP 578 audit hooks (sys.addaudithook), exploring their architectural design, runtime inspection capabilities, and bypasses.
talks.summary:
The Introduction of Python Audit Hooks (PEP 578)

Python 3.8 introduced audit hooks to provide security tools and system administrators with runtime visibility into sensitive operations like code compilation, network sockets, and dynamic imports.

Deconstructing Python Runtime Security Architecture

Leron Gray explains the CPython internal implementation of `sys.addaudithook` and `PySys_Audit`, examining what system events are logged.

Evaluating Bypass Vectors and Memory Manipulation

The author explores techniques for tampering with runtime structures in memory—including ctypes abuse, hooking C-level function pointers, and disabling callback arrays.

Designing Robust Python Runtime Defenses

The presentation discusses how application developers can effectively implement audit hooks and what limitations defenders must anticipate.

talks.title: Breaking the Attack Chain: Exploiting Structural Blindspots in Modern IT Operations
talks.teaser: Corey Ham and Matt Eidelberg analyze why targeted attack chains succeed, exploiting systemic blindspots between IT operations and security monitoring.
talks.summary:
The Friction Between IT Administration and Security Controls

Even in mature enterprise environments, operational compromises made for business convenience create structural blindspots that red teams routinely exploit.

Dissecting Realistic Attack Chains from Initial Access to Domain Takeover

Corey Ham and Matt Eidelberg walk through full attack chains—abusing service accounts, shared local administrator passwords, and unmonitored legacy subnets.

Exploiting Administrative Tooling for Living-Off-The-Land

The speakers illustrate how adversaries turn legitimate management tools (PowerShell remoting, WMI, PsExec) into covert lateral movement vectors.

Actionable Strategies for Breaking the Attack Chain

The authors present practical architectural reforms—including Tiered Administration, privileged access workstations, and focused telemetry auditing.

talks.title: Red Teaming: Born from the Hacking Community
talks.teaser: L0pht Heavy Industries co-founder Chris Wysopal (Weld Pond) reflects on the historical origins of red teaming and its evolution from grassroots hacker culture.
talks.summary:
Chris Wysopal (Weld Pond), co-founder of L0pht Heavy Industries and Veracode, explores the history and evolution of red teaming from early hacker roots to modern enterprise offensive operations. He reflects on how early hacker collectives in the 1990s pioneered vulnerability research, forced vendors to confront insecure software architectures, and laid the groundwork for today's adversarial testing frameworks.

Wysopal recounts early industry skepticism and vendor pushback against independent security research at 06:02 and 09:49. He explains how the adversarial mindset—refusing to accept trust assumptions and aggressively chaining minor flaws—became formalized into professional red teaming at 11:45 and 17:42. He discusses navigating corporate culture, negotiating scope with leadership (19:44), and demonstrating real-world business impact by emulating actual adversary tactics rather than relying on compliance checklists.

(AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Back to the Future: Computer Science, System Biology, & Molecular Code Injection
talks.teaser: Noa Novogroder explores parallels between computer science and molecular biology, showing how viruses executed code injection in biological cells 1.5 billion years ago.
talks.summary:
The Interdisciplinary Parallels of Computation and Biology

Biological cellular systems and computer architectures both execute stored algorithmic instructions, parse information sequences, and defend against malicious injection.

Biological Code Injection: Viruses and Retroviruses

Noa Novogroder examines how biological viruses inject foreign genetic bytecode into host cellular machinery, operating as nature's original living-off-the-land malware.

Decoding Mechanisms in Molecular Gene Expression

The author compares ribosome decoding pipelines and error correction mechanisms to compiler parsing, instruction interpreters, and system integrity verification.

Lessons for Cyber Defense from Biological Evolution

The presentation inspires cybersecurity researchers to study immune systems and biological resilience when architecting next-generation adaptive defenses.

talks.title: Autonomous Security Analysis & Penetration Testing Frameworks
talks.teaser: Dr. Ankur Chowdhary discusses autonomous penetration testing frameworks using attack graphs and reinforcement learning to plan and execute attack paths.
talks.summary:
The Human Bottleneck in Penetration Testing

Manual penetration testing requires extensive human expertise and time, making comprehensive, frequent assessments across expanding enterprise networks difficult.

Developing Autonomous Penetration Testing Engines

Dr. Ankur Chowdhary explores using attack graphs and Markov Decision Processes (MDPs) to model network state transitions and automate exploit planning.

Applying Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Attack Paths

The speaker demonstrates how autonomous agents learn optimal multi-step attack strategies by probing simulated networks and adapting to defensive responses.

Evaluating the Future of Automated Cyber Defense and Offense

The presentation discusses the integration of autonomous testing tools into continuous purple teaming and security validation pipelines.

talks.title: Automating Threat Hunting on the Dark Web: Tor Scraping & Credential Harvesting
talks.teaser: Apurv Gautam demonstrates building automated crawlers and threat intelligence collectors to monitor Tor darknet markets and paste sites for leaked corporate data.
talks.summary:
The Value of Dark Web Telemetry in Enterprise Threat Intelligence

Underground cybercrime forums, paste sites, and darknet leak platforms serve as early indicators of compromised employee credentials and corporate breach data.

Architecting Automated Tor Crawlers and Scrapers

Apurv Gautam details building resilient automated scraping frameworks in Python using Tor proxies, rotating user agents, and CAPTCHA handling.

Extracting, Parsing, and Normalizing Leaked Indicators

The speaker shows how to extract email domains, hashed credentials, and proprietary code snippets from unstructured forum posts and indexed onion pages.

Operationalizing Dark Web Feeds for Threat Hunting

The presentation provides incident responders with methodologies for integrating darknet intelligence into automated SIEM alerting and proactive credential resets.

talks.title: ATTPwn: An Open-Source Framework for Adversarial Emulation
talks.teaser: Pablo González presents ATTPwn, an open-source adversary emulation framework designed to automate MITRE ATT&CK techniques and validate defensive controls.
talks.summary:
The Need for Accessible Adversary Emulation Tooling

Validating security control efficacy requires automated tooling that accurately simulates real-world threat actor techniques without complex commercial licensing.

Architecture of the ATTPwn Framework

Pablo González introduces ATTPwn, an open-source platform that structures adversary emulation campaigns around mapped MITRE ATT&CK techniques.

Executing Dynamic Attack Plans and Evaluating Telemetry

The author demonstrates orchestrating automated multi-step attack simulations—including credential dumping, persistence, and discovery—across endpoint fleets.

Improving SOC Detection Engineering with Empirical Data

The presentation shows how purple teams leverage ATTPwn execution logs to identify detection gaps and refine SIEM/EDR alert rules.

talks.title: APTs Love PowerShell, You Should Too: Modern Offensive PowerShell Tradecraft
talks.teaser: Anthony Rose and Jake Krasnov debunk the myth that PowerShell is dead for red teams, showing how modern adversaries weaponize PowerShell while evading AMSI and logging.
talks.summary:
The Misconception of PowerShell's Demise

Despite the rise of C# and Go tooling, advanced persistent threat (APT) actors continue to heavily utilize PowerShell due to its native deep integration with Windows internals.

Deconstructing Modern PowerShell Security Controls

Anthony Rose and Jake Krasnov analyze Script Block Logging, Constrained Language Mode (CLM), and the Antimalware Scan Interface (AMSI).

Bypassing AMSI and Logging Protections in Memory

The speakers demonstrate practical in-memory patching techniques to disable AMSI scanning and blind Script Block Logging without administrative privileges.

Offensive Automation and Living-Off-The-Land Techniques

The authors showcase weaponizing native cmdlets for Active Directory reconnaissance, credential harvesting, and lateral movement.

talks.title: Catch Me If You Can: Stealthy Backdoor Deployment & Enterprise Persistence
talks.teaser: Eduardo Arriols breaks down stealthy backdoor deployment and persistent access techniques across enterprise Windows networks, evading blue team hunts.
talks.summary:
The Critical Challenge of Long-Term Persistence

Maintaining reliable, covert access during extended red team engagements requires deploying diverse persistence mechanisms that withstand reboots and blue team remediation.

Categorizing Modern Enterprise Persistence Mechanisms

Eduardo Arriols examines various persistence locations—including scheduled tasks, WMI event subscriptions, service creation, and registry run keys.

Implementing Stealthy C2 Channels and Fallback Implants

The author demonstrates configuring redundant, low-and-slow command and control (C2) implants that wake up periodically to avoid behavioral detection.

Blue Team Threat Hunting and Persistence Auditing

The presentation provides defenders with telemetry inspection checklists, AutoRuns analysis workflows, and detection heuristics to root out hidden implants.

talks.title: Bypassing Multi-Factor Authentication with Real-Time Session Replay Proxies
talks.teaser: Justin Hutchens demonstrates bypassing Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) using real-time adversary-in-the-middle reverse proxies to capture authenticated session tokens.
talks.summary:
The Evolution of Phishing Beyond Password Harvesting

With organizations broadly enforcing Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA), traditional credential harvesting phishing landing pages are no longer sufficient for initial access.

Architecture of Adversary-in-the-Middle (AiTM) Proxies

Justin Hutchens breaks down how reverse-proxy frameworks (e.g., Evilginx) intercept live authentication traffic between victims and legitimate identity providers.

Stealing Authenticated Session Cookies and Tokens in Real Time

The speaker illustrates how proxying legitimate MFA prompts allows attackers to harvest post-authentication session cookies, bypassing TOTP and push notifications.

Defensive Countermeasures: FIDO2 and Conditional Access

The presentation explores robust defensive mitigations—including hardware-bound FIDO2/WebAuthn keys, certificate-based authentication, and continuous token evaluation.

talks.title: Bypassing Security Controls in Mobile Networks from a Red Team Perspective
talks.teaser: Ali Abdollahi analyzes cellular core network security mechanisms, reviewing IMSI catchers, diameter routing flaws, and protocol bypasses from a red team perspective.
talks.summary:
The Expanding Core Architecture of Mobile Networks

Modern 4G LTE and 5G mobile networks implement complex cryptographic handshakes and mutual authentication protocols to secure subscriber traffic.

Analyzing Telecom Protocols and Signaling Boundaries

Ali Abdollahi investigates signaling protocols (SS7, Diameter, GTP), identifying how perimeter interconnection nodes leak location telemetry and subscriber identifiers.

Simulating Cellular Attacks and Perimeter Bypasses

The author demonstrates practical adversary techniques—including rogue base station interaction, IMSI harvesting, and data interception across unencrypted backhaul links.

Carrier Hardening and Telemetry Monitoring

The presentation provides telecom operators with recommendations for deploying signaling firewalls, protocol sanitization, and subscriber privacy enhancements.

talks.title: Protecting Wi-Fi Beacons from Outside Forgeries: Beacon Protection & Dragonblood
talks.teaser: Security researcher Mathy Vanhoef demonstrates attacks possible via spoofed Wi-Fi beacons and explores emerging beacon protection standards in WPA3.
talks.summary:
The Vulnerability of Unauthenticated 802.11 Beacons

Wi-Fi access points periodically broadcast unencrypted beacon frames to announce network capabilities, SSIDs, operating channels, and cryptographic ciphers.

Demonstrating Beacon Spoofing and Channel Confusion Attacks

Mathy Vanhoef illustrates how rogue actors inject forged beacon frames to manipulate victim power-save modes, downgrade cipher suites, and force rogue network roaming.

Analyzing WPA3 Beacon Protection Standards (802.11w / 802.11mc)

The author explores cryptographic beacon protection mechanisms designed to sign management frames and authenticate beacon contents.

Implementing Robust Wireless Defenses

The presentation outlines how operating systems and wireless access points can deploy beacon integrity verification to block rogue AP attacks.

talks.title: Password Cracking Beyond 15 Characters on a Budget Under $500
talks.teaser: Travis Palmer demonstrates advanced password cracking strategies tailored against 15+ character enterprise passphrase policies using sub-$500 GPU rigs.
talks.summary:
The Shifting Paradigm of Password Length Requirements

As organizations increase minimum password length policies to 15 or more characters, traditional brute-force and short mask attacks become computationally infeasible.

Building a Cost-Effective GPU Cracking Rig Under $500

Travis Palmer shares hardware blueprints for assembling high-throughput, affordable password cracking hardware using consumer GPUs and second-hand components.

Designing Targeted Passphrase and Grammar Mask Attacks

Palmer details modeling human passphrase generation habits, combining wordlists, grammar templates, and combinatorial rules (Hashcat/John the Ripper) to crack long passphrases.

Revising Enterprise Authentication Guidelines

The presentation provides guidance for security teams on evaluating password entropy and migrating to multi-factor authentication and passkeys.

talks.title: OU Having a Laugh: Abusing Organizational Unit DACLs in Active Directory
talks.teaser: Petros Koutrompis analyzes newly added BloodHound edges targeting Active Directory Organizational Units (OUs), demonstrating subtle ACL takeover paths.
talks.summary:
The Power of Active Directory Attack Path Graphing

BloodHound has transformed enterprise assessments by mapping complex graph relationships and hidden discretionary access control lists (DACLs) across Active Directory.

Analyzing Organizational Unit (OU) Permission Structures

Petros Koutrompis dissects how generic write permissions and object creation rights over OUs can be weaponized to seize control of child objects.

Chaining OU DACL Abuse into Domain Escalation

The speaker demonstrates real-world attack paths where low-privilege users manipulate OU permissions to move computer accounts, force GPO updates, and compromise administrators.

Defensive Auditing and DACL Hygiene

The author provides remediation queries and auditing scripts to identify and remove dangerous inherited permissions on Active Directory containers.

talks.title: Offensive Embedded Exploitation: From Hardware Interfaces to Root Shells
talks.teaser: Kaustubh provides a comprehensive walkthrough of offensive embedded IoT device exploitation, covering UART/JTAG probing, firmware extraction, and memory corruption.
talks.summary:
The Proliferation of Connected Embedded Devices

Smart consumer appliances, industrial gateways, and medical IoT devices integrate embedded Linux microcontrollers that frequently lack basic physical and software protections.

Hardware Interface Probing: UART, JTAG, and SPI

Kaustubh demonstrates identifying physical debug interfaces on printed circuit boards, connecting logic analyzers, and dumping SPI flash memory chips.

Firmware Reverse Engineering and Root Filesystem Extraction

The author walks through unpacking proprietary firmware images using binwalk, analyzing squashfs filesystems, and discovering hardcoded root credentials and backdoors.

Memory Corruption and Service Exploitation

The presentation details finding buffer overflows in embedded HTTP and Telnet daemons, cross-compiling payloads, and spawning interactive root shells.

talks.title: Modern Red Team Tradecraft: Bridging the Gap with Real-World Espionage
talks.teaser: Sajal Thomas examines the technical gap between commercial red teams and state-sponsored APT groups, sharing advanced tradecraft to elevate offensive testing.
talks.summary:
The Evolving Landscape of Threat Actor Sophistication

Nation-state cyber espionage groups operate with patience, bespoke infrastructure, and zero-day tooling that traditional penetration tests rarely replicate.

Bridging the Methodology Gap in Red Teaming

Sajal Thomas analyzes advanced operational concepts—including domain fronting alternatives, long-dwell in-memory persistence, and operational risk mitigation.

Executing Covert Lateral Movement and Data Staging

The speaker demonstrates navigating complex enterprise networks using living-off-the-land techniques without generating anomalous endpoint security telemetry.

Elevating Enterprise Resilience Through Realistic Simulations

The presentation encourages red teams to shift from speed-based pwning to realistic, objective-driven adversary emulation that truly tests detection engineering.

talks.title: Mechanizing Methodology: Automating Attack Surface Discovery & Reconnaissance
talks.teaser: Daniel Miessler presents strategies for mechanizing security methodologies, automating continuous asset discovery and attack surface management.
talks.summary:
The Human Bottleneck in Attack Surface Discovery

While hundreds of specialized reconnaissance tools exist, executing a rigorous security methodology consistently across massive target domains is mentally exhausting.

Introducing Methodological Mechanization

Daniel Miessler outlines frameworks for translating human discovery heuristics and checklists into automated, modular execution pipelines.

Continuous Asset Monitoring and Differential Alerting

The author demonstrates chaining DNS enumeration, port scanning, web screenshotting, and technology fingerprinting into continuous background discovery engines.

Maximizing Security Analyst Efficiency

The presentation shares open-source tooling concepts and architectural guidance to help bug hunters and red teamers automate repetitive reconnaissance.

talks.title: Kubernetes Goat: A Vulnerable by Design Cluster for Learning Cloud Native Security
talks.teaser: Madhu Akula introduces Kubernetes Goat, an intentionally vulnerable cluster environment designed to learn Kubernetes security, RBAC misconfigurations, and container escapes.
talks.summary:
The Complexity of Cloud Native Security

Kubernetes orchestrates enterprise container workloads worldwide, but its vast API surface, complex RBAC controls, and network policies create severe security challenges.

Introducing the Kubernetes Goat Playground

Madhu Akula presents Kubernetes Goat, an open-source vulnerable-by-design environment mapping real-world cloud native security misconfigurations.

Hands-On Attack Scenarios and Cluster Compromise

Akula walks through practical attack scenarios—including SSRF in containerized web apps, exposed Docker/Kubelet sockets, RBAC token privilege escalation, and host breakout.
